sources.name: Gemini Apps Help: Generate and edit images
Google Gemini: AI image generator and photo editor

caption:
Nano Banana 2 is the free image model inside Gemini.
It makes new pictures and edits your own photos from one sentence.

What would you edit first?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Google · Photo: Nicholas Sutrich / Android Central
threads_text: Gemini's free image model, Nano Banana 2, can swap a background, fix one part of a photo or merge several pictures into one. The trick is to start with a verb and describe the subject, the action and the setting. What would you edit first?

slides.headline: How to use *Nano Banana* in Gemini for free: 5 prompts that work

slides.heading: 1. Start with a *verb*
paras: Google's own tip: start with draw, generate or create, then name a style, the subject, what it does and the setting.
slides.prompt: Create a photorealistic image of a golden retriever reading a newspaper on a park bench in autumn, soft morning light.

slides.heading: 2. Change *one part* of a photo
paras: Upload your photo and say exactly what to change. Nano Banana 2 is built for local edits.
slides.prompt: Keep everything the same, but replace the gray sky with a clear sunset and remove the trash can on the left.

slides.heading: 3. Merge *several photos*
paras: Upload a few pictures and ask Gemini to build one new image from them. It keeps faces consistent.
slides.prompt: Put the person from the first photo and the dog from the second photo together on the beach from the third photo.

slides.heading: 4. Make *text* that reads right
paras: Nano Banana 2 renders text much better than older models, so invitations and posters work.
slides.prompt: Design a birthday invitation that says "Maya turns 30" with "Saturday, 7 PM" below it, watercolor flowers, cream background.

slides.heading: 5. Borrow a *style*
paras: Add a reference picture and ask Gemini to apply its colors, texture or mood to your subject.
slides.prompt: Use the colors and mood of the second image for the portrait in the first image. Keep the face exactly the same.

site_article.headline: How to use Gemini Nano Banana for free: edit and create images
site_article.dek: Nano Banana 2 is the image model inside the free Gemini app. Here is how to make a picture, edit your own photo and get better results with prompts you can copy.
site_article.summary: Nano Banana 2 is Google's default image model in the Gemini app and the free choice for creating and editing pictures. Paid Google AI plans add Nano Banana Pro and higher limits.
site_article.seo_title: How to use Gemini Nano Banana for free: edit and create images
site_article.seo_description: How to use Nano Banana in Gemini for free: make images, edit your own photos, merge pictures, download them, plus 6 prompts to copy and the limits to know.
site_article.answer_summary: Go to gemini.google.com, open the sidebar, choose Images and type a prompt that starts with a verb. To edit a photo, upload it and describe the change. Nano Banana 2 is the free default model.
site_article.hero_alt: A Google Pixel phone with the Gemini app open on its screen.

paragraphs.text: If you want to know how to use Gemini Nano Banana for free, the short answer is that you already have it. Nano Banana 2 is the default image model in the Gemini app, and Google's product page describes it as the free model for making and editing images. Google introduced it on February 26, 2026, built on Gemini 3.1 Flash Image, and said it replaced Nano Banana Pro across the Fast, Thinking and Pro modes in the app.

It does two jobs. It creates new pictures from a text prompt, and it edits pictures you upload: change a background, swap an object, add something, or combine several photos into one. Google lists better text inside images, consistent characters across images and edits to one part of a photo as its main strengths.
What you need before you start

You need a Google account signed in to Gemini. Google's help page says image editing is not available to users under 18, and the feature is limited to the countries and languages where the Gemini app works. Work and school accounts can have different rules or no access at all.

The free plan has a daily limit. Google does not publish the exact number on its help page; it only says that limits apply and that paid Google AI plans get higher ones. Paid subscribers can also redo an image with Nano Banana Pro, the slower model meant for images that need more detail and more precise control.
How to make your first image with Nano Banana

paragraphs.title: 1. Open Gemini
paragraphs.text: Go to gemini.google.com on a computer, or open the Gemini app on your phone, and sign in.

paragraphs.title: 2. Open Images
paragraphs.text: On the web, click Open Sidebar, then Images. You can pick one of the ready-made templates or type your own prompt.

paragraphs.title: 3. Write the prompt
paragraphs.text: Start with a verb such as create, draw or generate. Then say the style, the subject, what the subject is doing and where. One clear sentence beats a list of keywords.

paragraphs.title: 4. Download it
paragraphs.text: Hover over the finished image and click Download full size. You can also click More under the image and choose Export to Docs if you want to keep working on it in a document.

The model you pick in Gemini decides which image model runs. According to Google's help page, Flash-Lite uses Nano Banana 2 Lite, which is quick but not made for several reference images or repeated edits. Flash and Pro use Nano Banana 2. So for editing work, switch away from Flash-Lite before you ask for the image.
How to edit your own photo

paragraphs.title: 1. Upload the picture
paragraphs.text: Start a chat in Gemini and add your photo with the upload button. You can add several pictures at once if you want Gemini to combine them.

paragraphs.title: 2. Describe only the change
paragraphs.text: Say what should stay the same and what should change. Be concrete: which object, which side of the picture, which color.

paragraphs.title: 3. Keep editing in the same chat
paragraphs.text: Ask for one fix at a time. For an image you made earlier, open Library in the sidebar, click the image, click Chat under it and type the next change.

Tom's Guide reported in December 2025 that the Gemini app lets you draw or circle on an uploaded photo to mark the spot you want changed, with or without a text prompt. Google's help page does not describe this tool, so if you do not see it, describe the spot in words instead.
Gemini Nano Banana prompts to copy

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: A clean first image
paragraphs.text: Create a photorealistic image of [subject] [doing what] in [place], [time of day] light, shot from [angle].

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: Fix one part of a photo
paragraphs.text: Keep everything in this photo exactly the same, but replace [the thing to change] with [the new thing]. Do not change the faces.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 3: Combine photos
paragraphs.text: Put the person from the first image and the [pet or object] from the second image together in the setting from the third image. Natural lighting, same style as the third image.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 4: Text that reads right
paragraphs.text: Design a [poster, invitation or card] that says "[exact words]" in large letters, with "[smaller line]" below it. Style: [watercolor, retro, minimal]. Background: [color].

paragraphs.title: Prompt 5: Borrow a style
paragraphs.text: Apply the colors, texture and mood of the second image to the subject in the first image. Keep the subject's shape and face unchanged.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 6: A new format
paragraphs.text: Turn this image into a [9:16 vertical, 16:9 wide or square] version. Extend the background naturally and keep the subject centered.

Google's own page lists changing the mood, lighting, camera angle or focus of a photo, and adjusting a picture to a different aspect ratio, as things the model handles. Those make good first experiments because the result is easy to judge.
Where Nano Banana needs help

Google's help page itself points to the weak spots: the Lite model is not built for several references or repeated edits, and the free plan has a daily cap. In practice that means short, specific requests work best. Split a big edit into steps, tell the model what to keep as well as what to change, and when a result is close, ask for one fix instead of starting over so you do not spend your daily images.

Every image is marked as AI-made. Google says each picture carries an invisible SynthID watermark and a visible watermark, and that you can upload an image to the Gemini app and ask whether Google AI made it. Google may also remove images whose prompts break its terms or its prohibited use policy.
If you pay for a Google AI plan and an image needs finer detail or cleaner text, click More at the bottom right of the image and choose Redo with Pro. Free users stay on Nano Banana 2.

Nano Banana 2 is not only in the Gemini app. Google said it is also the default in AI Mode and Lens in Search and in its Flow creative studio, where it costs zero credits, and Engadget noted it can keep the look of up to five characters consistent in one workflow.
